subject: general
question: When was the National Rural Health Mission (NRHM) launched by the Government of India?
solution:
The correct answer is __** Apr 12 2005**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The National Rural Health Mission (NRHM)** was launched by the **Government of India** on **April 12, 2005**. It aimed to provide accessible, affordable, and quality healthcare to the rural population, especially vulnerable groups.
 
• The mission was introduced as part of the **National Health Policy** to address deficiencies in healthcare infrastructure and improve health indicators like **infant mortality rate** and **maternal mortality rate**.
 
• NRHM primarily targeted **18 states** where health indicators were particularly poor. These included states like **Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh**, and others.
 
• The mission focused on strengthening the public health system through interventions like **ASHA (Accredited Social Health Activist)**, improving infrastructure, and integrating primary, secondary, and tertiary healthcare services.
 
• NRHM also worked on improving **sanitation, nutrition, and safe drinking water** as complementary health interventions. It sought to reduce gaps in healthcare access between urban and rural areas.
 
• The mission emphasized **community participation** and introduced mechanisms for decentralization to empower local health facilities and improve their functionality.
 
• The **Janani Suraksha Yojana**, a key component of NRHM, aimed to promote institutional deliveries and reduce maternal and infant mortality rates.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Tue Apr 12 2005.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Objectives of NRHM:**

 
 
• **Strengthening rural healthcare infrastructure:** Building new health facilities like **Primary Health Centres (PHCs)**, **Community Health Centres (CHCs)**, and sub-centres.
 
• **Human resources:** Recruiting healthcare workers, including **ASHA workers**, nurses, and doctors, to fill gaps in rural health services.
 
• **Disease control:** Strengthening programs for communicable diseases like **malaria, tuberculosis, and HIV/AIDS**, as well as non-communicable diseases.
 
 
 
• **Key Features:**
 
 
• **ASHA workers:** Serving as a bridge between the healthcare system and the community, these workers provided essential health services and promoted awareness.
 
• **Decentralization:** Empowering **local governing bodies** like Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs) to plan and implement health initiatives.
 
• **Janani Suraksha Yojana:** Financial incentives for institutional deliveries to reduce maternal and infant mortality.
 
 
 
• **Achievements:**
 
 
• **Increased institutional deliveries:** A rise in institutional deliveries was observed across states due to programs like **Janani Suraksha Yojana**.
 
• **Improved health indicators:** Significant improvements were seen in **infant mortality rate**, **maternal mortality rate**, and life expectancy.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **NRHM's integration:** In 2013, NRHM was subsumed under the **National Health Mission (NHM)**, which also included the **National Urban Health Mission (NUHM)**.
 
• **Focus Areas:** NRHM prioritized **maternal health, child health, family planning, communicable diseases**, and infrastructure development.
 
• **Funding Mechanism:** The mission received funding through a mix of **central and state government contributions**, ensuring shared responsibility.
